Introduction

IZ*ONE (pronounced "eyes one") was a twelve-member project girl group formed through the survival show "Produce 48," the third installment of the Mnet Produce franchise. The group brought together 48 South Korean trainees and 48 Japanese idols from the AKB48 group and its sister groups. IZ*ONE's members promoted for two and a half years under Off The Record Entertainment and Swing Entertainment, with a special contract set to end in 2021.

"Produce 48" aired from June 15 to August 31, 2018, culminating in the live broadcast of the final episode. The twelve most-voted contestants became members of IZ*ONE, with Jang Wonyoung ranking first and becoming the center. The other members were Miyawaki Sakura (second), Jo Yuri (third), Choi Yena (fourth), An Yujin (fifth), Yabuki Nako (sixth), Kwon Eunbi (seventh), Kang Hyewon (eighth), Honda Hitomi (ninth), Kim Chaewon (tenth), Kim Minju (eleventh), and Lee Chaeyeon (twelfth). Some of the members had prior experience in the industry, including Sakura and Nako from HKT48, Hitomi from AKB48, and Eunbi, who was previously part of Ye-A under the stage name "Kazoo."

On September 21, 2018, IZ*ONE's management in South Korea was transferred to Off The Record Entertainment, replacing Pledis Entertainment. The group debuted on October 29, 2018, with the mini album "COLOR*IZ." On the same day, their official fandom name, "WIZ*ONE," was revealed, derived from the word "wizard," symbolizing fans who are creating a magical future together with the group.

In late 2019, IZ*ONE went on hiatus due to a rigging controversy surrounding the "Produce" series. CJ ENM's CEO, Heo Min Heoi, publicly apologized on December 30, 2019, stating that the company would compensate those affected by the incident and work on resuming the group's activities. IZ*ONE resumed promotions in February 2020.

The group officially disbanded on April 28, 2021, after completing their two and a half years of promotional activities.
